goal.request: Prevent reverse-image prompts from normalizing a source-relative pose toward centered or frontal alignment when individual pose axes were discarded with weak evidence or when a seemingly neutral spatial clause implicitly actuates additional axes.

evidence.claim: After the previous skill improvement and a new generation, the user still judged the subject pose as centered and frontal and questioned whether the skill had actually improved.
evidence.artifact: Conversation feedback on 2026-08-26: 이번에도 여전히 자세는 가운데 정면인 것 같은데

evidence.claim: The motivating source contains a low-view human whose visible head, torso, shoulder, and side-depth relations must be assessed jointly rather than replaced by an assumed neutral alignment.
The delivered post-improvement render presents the human with a strongly centered, near-frontal global pose, matching the user's reported failure.

The exact delivered prompt positively actuates centered, upper-center, almost-vertical, and nearly-frontal alignment even though the source-relative turn is expressed only as slight. Those clauses jointly pull placement, principal-axis, torso, head/body, and shoulder relations.

The motivating plan classified torso yaw, torso roll, head/body lateral offset, and shoulder slope as not-material, recorded no coupled spatial effect, and still bound prompt controls containing positive neutral-alignment language.
evidence.artifact: /tmp/reverse-image-independent.Wh2cdC/plan.json decisions and emitted controls; motivating source-bound analysis artifact

evidence.claim: The preceding compact pose/light improvement claimed only structural implementation and explicitly left prompt, render, and user layers unscored; the new user judgment therefore revises any inferred render-level success rather than contradicting its bounded package claim.

The spatial-orientation/v5 validator and source-neutral fixtures pass for isolated non-emission evidence, low-confidence and confounded handling, coupled ownership, exact prompt-effect audit coverage, implicit non-invariant actuation rejection, genuinely centered invariants, opposite and mirrored directions, and compiled package consistency.
evidence.artifact: python3 -m unittest discover -s skills/reverse-image-prompt/tests -p test_*.py => 254 passed; validate_modules.py => 37 modules, 6 lanes, 16596 runtime words, 3748 Tier-0 words, duplicate ratio 0.0014; gen_manifest.py --check => pass; git diff --check => pass

perceptual_contract.primary_success_condition: A final spatial clause may not pull the subject toward any alignment that lacks source-owned invariant or coupled evidence, and a pose axis may not be discarded merely because its individual cue is weak or confounded.
perceptual_contract.user_appeal: Preserve the source's particular off-axis pose relationship instead of returning another centered, frontal result.

invariants.statement: Every flexible or not-material spatial axis passes a structured single-dimension neutralization test with adjacent relations held fixed and names what remains preserved.
Low-confidence or wholly confounded axes become uncertain unless one invariant coupled effect owns their joint visible result.
Every exact emitted spatial control declares both explicit and implicit affected decisions, includes its individual owner or all coupled members, and emits only with a source-consistent verdict.
Centered, offset, frontal, oblique, opposed, and either mirrored direction remain valid only when the current source supports and owns them; none is installed as a runtime default.
causal_controls: no adjective blacklist or preferred pose

flexible_dimensions: the source-supported direction or degree of every spatial axis
whether an effect is individually resolved or coupled
the literal spatial wording after complete effect audit
downstream generator variation after the validated prompt

mismatches.source_state: The source-visible pose depends on interacting low-view, torso, head/body, shoulder, and side-depth relations whose individual physical attribution may be weak.
mismatches.render_state: The delivered render reads as centered and frontal after the prompt explicitly reinforced centered, vertical, upright, and nearly-frontal alignment.

hypotheses.statement: Free-form non-emission reasons let weak or confounded pose axes be labeled not-material without testing whether neutralizing that one axis changes adjacent visible relations.
hypotheses.falsifier: Held-out plans with structured isolated neutralization behave no differently from shallow non-emission prose across weak, confounded, and genuinely non-material axes.

hypotheses.statement: Alignment-style prose that looks compositional can positively actuate several pose and viewpoint axes, so checking only its declared owner permits a later clause to normalize unsupported relations.
hypotheses.falsifier: Unrelated prompt comparisons show that clauses with the same declared owner but different implicit spatial effects produce no systematic axis pull and never override source-relative pose controls.

hypotheses.statement: Package and route validity cannot establish prompt, pixel, or user-level fidelity; the prior structural intervention needed post-generation user evidence before any stronger success claim.
hypotheses.falsifier: Structural validation alone reliably predicts the user's pose judgment on unrelated delivered renders without prompt or pixel evaluation.

intervention.general_rule: Use spatial-orientation/v5. A flexible or not-material axis requires a preserved single-dimension neutralization test with adjacent decisions held fixed. Low-confidence or wholly confounded axes become uncertain unless one invariant coupled effect preserves their joint result. Every exact spatial control audits all explicit and implicit affected decisions and emits only when each is individually invariant or coupled and the net verdict is source-consistent.
intervention.generalization_basis: The intervention is parameterized only by generic spatial dimensions, source-owned cue ids, confidence, confounders, decision ownership, coupled membership, and exact prompt excerpts. It encodes no motivating side, angle, garment, body configuration, coordinate, adjective ban, or preferred centered versus off-center outcome, and held-out fixtures exercise centered, opposite, mirrored, individual, coupled, and non-human cases.

decision.rationale: The earliest observed failure is now guarded at both non-emission representation and final spatial-clause actuation. Source-neutral package fixtures pass and the preceding structural change is explicitly revised at the untested render/user boundary. No independent post-change prompt extraction, new render, or post-change user review was performed in this turn, so the result is implemented structurally rather than promoted as prompt or pixel fidelity.
